numbering: IEEE references ordered by first citation in report.md.
scope: Primary sources supporting the existing methods, evaluation interpretation, and planned controlled experiments. A cited paper motivates a hypothesis; it does not establish performance on cassette-front two-keypoint pose.

entries.title: Data README

entries.supported_claim: The data specification uses the cassette_front class and two lower front corners ordered by image x-coordinate, with flip_idx [1, 0]; an unavailable corner is encoded as 0 0 0 rather than guessed.
entries.limitation: This is the upstream annotation contract, not evidence of an application's accuracy, a fully specified box-extent policy, or a requirement to output inferred coordinates for invisible corners.

entries.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
entries.venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Redmon, S. Divvala, R. Girshick, and A. Farhadi, “You only look once: Unified, real-time object detection,” in Proc. IEEE Conf. Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR), 2016, pp. 779–788, doi: 10.1109/CVPR.2016.91.
entries.supported_claim: The original YOLO formulates object detection as a single network that predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities from a complete image.
entries.limitation: This historical detector paper does not document the current pose implementation, its two-point output, or the accuracy of the cassette models.

supports: DOI in indexed primary IEEE record

entries.title: TIDE: A General Toolbox for Identifying Object Detection Errors
entries.ieee_entry: D. Bolya, S. Foley, J. Hays, and J. Hoffman, “TIDE: A general toolbox for identifying object detection errors,” in Computer Vision – ECCV 2020, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 12348. Springer, 2020, pp. 558–573, doi: 10.1007/978-3-030-58580-8_33.
entries.supported_claim: TIDE separates sources of object-detection and instance-segmentation error and measures their effects on average precision, encouraging diagnosis beyond a single aggregate score.
entries.limitation: The project's fixed-threshold missed, unmatched, and duplicate counts are not a full reproduction of TIDE's error-oracle analysis, and corner accuracy requires additional metrics.

entries.title: ObjectLab: Automated Diagnosis of Mislabeled Images in Object Detection Data
entries.venue: ICML Workshop on Data-centric Machine Learning Research
entries.ieee_entry: U. Tkachenko, A. Thyagarajan, and J. Mueller, “ObjectLab: Automated diagnosis of mislabeled images in object detection data,” in ICML Workshop on Data-centric Machine Learning Research, 2023. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00832
entries.supported_claim: ObjectLab uses model predictions to prioritize images that may contain missing, misplaced, or incorrectly classified bounding-box annotations for human review.
entries.limitation: A model-generated suspicion is not proof that an annotation is wrong; independent image inspection is still required, and the paper does not validate the project's corner labels.
metadata_notes: No proceedings page range was verified, so none is supplied.
The arXiv DOI is not represented as a publisher proceedings DOI.

entries.title: Noise-Aware Evaluation of Object Detectors
entries.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Murrugarra-Llerena and C. R. Jung, “Noise-aware evaluation of object detectors,” in Proc. IEEE/CVF Winter Conf. Applications of Computer Vision (WACV), 2025, doi: 10.1109/WACV61041.2025.00903.
entries.supported_claim: Bounding-box annotation uncertainty can alter detector evaluation, particularly for small objects and restrictive overlap thresholds, motivating sensitivity analysis of disputed references.
entries.limitation: This does not justify moving reference annotations toward a preferred model's predictions or treating model agreement as ground truth.

supports: author names as printed on paper
DOI in indexed primary IEEE record

metadata_notes: CVF verifies pages 9304–9313. Secondary indexes give a different IEEE pagination; an IEEE page range was not verified from the primary record, so the DOI-based IEEE entry deliberately omits pages.

entries.title: Contrast Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization
entries.ieee_entry: K. Zuiderveld, “Contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization,” in Graphics Gems IV, P. S. Heckbert, Ed. Academic Press, 1994, pp. 474–485.
entries.supported_claim: CLAHE limits local histogram amplification by clipping and redistributing histogram counts, with interpolation between neighboring regions to reduce boundary artifacts.
entries.limitation: The chapter supplies the algorithmic background, not evidence that a particular clip limit or tile grid improves cassette detection or two-corner localization.

supports: chapter author and pages in indexed publisher record

entries.title: Image-Adaptive YOLO for Object Detection in Adverse Weather Conditions
entries.ieee_entry: W. Liu, G. Ren, R. Yu, S. Guo, J. Zhu, and L. Zhang, “Image-adaptive YOLO for object detection in adverse weather conditions,” in Proc. AAAI Conf. Artificial Intelligence, vol. 36, 2022, pp. 1792–1800, doi: 10.1609/aaai.v36i2.20072.
entries.supported_claim: IA-YOLO jointly trains an image-dependent filter-parameter predictor and a YOLOv3 detector for adverse-weather object detection.
entries.limitation: Joint learned enhancement differs from applying fixed CLAHE to a frozen pose model; the cassette CLAHE result cannot establish the value of the full IA-YOLO approach.

entries.title: Slicing Aided Hyper Inference and Fine-tuning for Small Object Detection
entries.venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP)
entries.ieee_entry: F. C. Akyon, S. O. Altinuc, and A. Temizel, “Slicing aided hyper inference and fine-tuning for small object detection,” in Proc. IEEE Int. Conf. Image Processing (ICIP), 2022, pp. 966–970, doi: 10.1109/ICIP46576.2022.9897990.
entries.supported_claim: SAHI combines predictions from image slices and studies sliced fine-tuning to improve small-object box detection in the evaluated datasets.
entries.limitation: Two-keypoint coordinate restoration, tile-edge truncation, and duplicate handling need separate validation; slicing is a different intervention from increasing whole-image input resolution.

entries.title: Simple Baselines for Human Pose Estimation and Tracking
entries.ieee_entry: B. Xiao, H. Wu, and Y. Wei, “Simple baselines for human pose estimation and tracking,” in Proc. European Conf. Computer Vision (ECCV), 2018, pp. 466–481. [Online]. Available: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_ECCV_2018/html/Bin_Xiao_Simple_Baselines_for_ECCV_2018_paper.html
entries.supported_claim: The human-pose baseline averages heatmaps from original and horizontally flipped inputs during testing, providing a direct pose-estimation precedent for flip testing.
entries.limitation: Its heatmap model and human-joint task differ from the project's two-point regression output, so its results do not establish a cassette improvement.
